barriers.description: Health care providers (eg, nurses) were not included in the standardized usability questionnaire, preventing designers from capturing provider perspectives on the care-provider app.
barriers.justification: Excluding providers limited the team's ability to facilitate user involvement and evaluate the care-provider app, hindering the HCD workloads of facilitating user involvement and evaluating designs.
barriers.reference_excerpt: As iCARE was in the testing stage, and the main focus of this study was to test the experience of patients and the usability of the patient app, and therefore, we did not include health care providers (such as nurses) to complete the Health-ITUES.

barriers.description: The team developed the apps only for Android initially and deferred iOS compatibility until the Android version was stable, limiting platform coverage during design and testing.
barriers.justification: Limiting development to Android constrained the designers' ability to understand context of use and to involve and evaluate users on other major platforms (iOS), impeding the workloads of understanding context of use and evaluating designs across device contexts.
barriers.reference_excerpt: The patient app and care provider app were developed to be compatible with Android-based smartphones, as they are more popular and affordable in China [27]. We will also develop iCARE to be compatible on iOS-based smartphones once the app is identified as being stable in Android-based smartphones.

barriers.description: A blood glucose monitor was not distributed to diabetic participants in stage II, so the team could not test glucose-monitoring integration with the app.
barriers.justification: Lack of device distribution prevented designers from evaluating the app's integration with glucose devices and from fully understanding context of use for diabetic patients, hindering the evaluation of designs and understanding of context of use.
barriers.reference_excerpt: As the blood glucose monitor was not distributed to patients with diabetes (10/61 patients) in stage II testing, it was not available for testing the differences in this regard.

barriers.description: A substantial number of eligible patients (n=40) refused to participate due to lack of time, schedule conflicts, or lack of interest, reducing available user input.
barriers.justification: Participant refusal limited designers' ability to recruit and involve end users for task analysis and usability evaluation, hindering the HCD workloads of facilitating user involvement and evaluating designs.
barriers.reference_excerpt: There were 40 patients eligible for the study but refused to participate due to various reasons, such as lack of time, conflict of schedule, or simply being uninterested.
